 Judgment

MFA No.201312/2018 is filed by the insurer challenging the quantum of compensation as well as the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation awarded by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kalaburagi, (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.143/2016 vide judgment and award dated 01.03.2018.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.200248/2019 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in terms of the said judgment and award.

3. The appellants in MFA No.200248/2019, who are respondent Nos.1 and 2 in MFA No.201312/2018, shall henceforth be referred to as 'claimants' while the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1268 respondent Nos.1 and 2 in MFA No.200248/2019, who are respondent Nos.3 and 4 in MFA No.201312/2018, shall henceforth be referred to as the 'rider' and 'owner' respectively of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 32/EA-9808 involved in the accident.
The respondent No.3 in MFA No.200248/2019, who is the appellant in MFA No.201312/2018 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'insurer' of the said motorcycle.
4. The claimants are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri Revanasiddappa.

They claimed that on 25.01.2014 at about 5.30 p..m., the deceased was going to his College to receive Industrial Training Institute (ITI) Degree certificate on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-33/L-8040 and when he was on N.H.218 Gulbarga- Jewargi road, near Sradagi Khani village, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/EA-9808 (henceforth referred to as 'the offending motorcycle') ridden from the opposite direction, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motorcycle.

As a result,
he NC: 2023:KHC-K:1268 suffered grievous injuries and died at the spot.

The claimants filed a claim petition contending that the death of Sri Revanasiddappa was due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending motorcycle and hence, claimed compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the rider, owner and insurer of the offending motorcycle.

sentences.text: The claim petition was contested by the rider and owner of the offending motorcycle.

They contended that the offending motorcycle was insured and the insurance policy was valid as on the date of the accident and hence, liability to pay compensation, if any, be fastened on the insurer.
6. The claim petition was contested by the insurer, who denied the contentions urged in the claim petition.

They also contended that the deceased and the rider of the offending motorcycle did not possess a valid licence and as such the insurer was not liable to indemnify the owner of the offending motorcycle.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1268 7.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and he marked documents as Exs.P1 to P8.
The insurer did not lead any oral evidence.
A copy of the policy of insurance is marked as Ex.R1 by consent.
8. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider.
It held that the death of the deceased was due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident.

9. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal noticed that the deceased was 19 years old at the time of the accident and therefore, his income was considered at a sum of Rs.6,000/- as claimed by the claimants.

It deducted 50% of the income of the deceased as he was a bachelor towards his personal expenses and awarded the following compensation:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1268 Sl. Heads of Amount No. Compensation
1. Love and affection Rs. 50,000-00 2. Funeral expenses and Rs. 15,000-00 Transportation charges 3. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,48,000-00 4. Loss of estate Rs. 15,000-00
Total compensation Rs. 7,28,000-00
In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, it held that the insurer of the offending motorcycle is liable to indemnify the owner of the offending motorcycle.
It directed the insurer of the offending motorcycle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.

10. In view of the finding of the Tribunal regarding liability and the quantum of compensation awarded by it, MFA No.201312/2018 is filed by the insurer and the claimants have preferred MFA No.200248/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the insurer contended that the claimants did not place on record any documents to establish that the deceased possessed a valid licence to drive the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-33/L- 8040.

He submits that the rider of the offending motorcycle did not possess a valid licence as on the date of the accident and therefore, there is a willful violation of the conditions of the policy of insurance which exonerated it from indemnifying the owner of the offending motorcycle.
12.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal did not factor loss of future prospects as the deceased had completed his ITI training and therefore, had enormous potential to be employed as a technician.
He also contended that the Tribunal failed to award adequate compensation towards the loss of filial consortium and therefore, prays that the compensation awarded be enhanced.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurer and the learned counsel for the claimants.
14. The accident and the consequent death of Sri Revanasiddappa in the accident is not much in dispute.

Though the insurer claimed that the deceased did not possess a valid licence and the driver of the offending motorcycle did not possess a licence, the insurer did not step into the witness box to prove its contention.
It did not make any effort to ascertain whether the deceased and the rider of the offending motorcycle possessed a licence or not.
Therefore, the contention of the insurer is not based on any material document.
Consequently, the ground urged by the insurer does not merit consideration.

In so far as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, the Tribunal ought to have considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- as prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in respect of persons who died in - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1268 accidents that happened in the year 2014 and must have factored loss of future prospects at 40% as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd.
v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and loss of filial consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others [(2018) 18 SCC 130].

However, the claimants/appellants in MFA No.200248/2019 shall not be entitled to interest for the delayed period of 241 days in filing the appeal.
